title: Every closed subscheme of a relative Proj over a quasi-compact base is itself a relative Proj of a graded quotient

standard_prerequisites.name: The relative Proj of a quasi-coherent graded algebra is separated, and pushforward along a quasi-compact separated morphism preserves quasi-coherence, cited from the constructions and schemes chapters
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the kernel of the canonical map of graded modules quasi-coherent, hence a legitimate graded quotient algebra.

standard_prerequisites.name: A surjection of quasi-coherent graded algebras induces an everywhere defined closed immersion of relative Proj's, cited from the constructions chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the closed subscheme Z' that has to be shown equal to Z.

standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-compactness of a Proj over an affine base in terms of finitely many homogeneous elements generating the irrelevant ideal, cited from the constructions chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the proof reduce the comparison of two closed subschemes to the affine charts D_+(f_i).

standard_prerequisites.name: Invertibility of the twists of the structure sheaf on Proj and the identification of the multiplication maps of twists of a quasi-coherent module as isomorphisms
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows homogeneous elements to be adjusted by powers of the chart equation without changing the ideal they generate.

core_obligations: Set up the quotient algebra: since the relative Proj is separated and the morphism is quasi-compact, the kernel of the canonical map from the graded algebra to the graded pushforward of the twists of the closed subscheme's structure sheaf is quasi-coherent, so the quotient is a quasi-coherent graded algebra, and the induced morphism from its relative Proj is an everywhere defined closed immersion; hence it suffices to show the two closed subschemes agree (proof lines 7919-7931).

Reduce to a comparison on affine charts: the question is local on the base, so assume the base affine and the Proj of a graded algebra over it; choose finitely many homogeneous elements generating the irrelevant ideal up to radical, so the Proj is covered by the corresponding standard affine opens, and it is enough to compare the two closed subschemes on each of these charts (proof lines 7933-7942).

One inclusion: with the two ideals J and J' of the chart's degree zero part, and d the least common multiple of the degrees of the chosen elements, the ideal J' is generated by elements g over f to a power with g homogeneous of the right degree; adjusting by powers of the chart equation one may assume the degree is divisible by d, and since g vanishes on the closed subscheme the corresponding quotient lies in J, so J' is contained in J (proof lines 7944-7963).

Converse inclusion: conversely, if a quotient of an adjusted element lies in J, then on each other chart the localization of J agrees with the localization of the local ideal J_i, which shows that a suitable multiple of that element by a power of the chart equation lies in the ideal I of the graded algebra, because its restriction to every chart vanishes on the closed subscheme; hence the quotient lies in J' and the two ideals agree (proof lines 7965-7983).
proof_roadmap: Produce the closed immersion from the relative Proj of the graded quotient defined by the kernel and reduce the claim to the equality of two closed subschemes (proof lines 7919-7931).

Work locally on the base and on the standard affine charts of a Proj, then prove the two inclusions between the defining ideals by adjusting homogeneous elements with powers of the chart equation and comparing localizations across charts (proof lines 7933-7983).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a quasi-compact relative Proj, every closed subscheme is the relative Proj of the graded quotient by the kernel of the canonical map to the graded pushforward of its structure sheaf's twists (statement lines 7903-7917). The counted proof is a genuine local computation: it first obtains the closed immersion from the candidate quotient algebra and reduces to identifying two closed subschemes, then works on affine charts of a Proj, where the two inclusions between the defining ideals are proved by adjusting homogeneous elements with powers of the chart equation (using invertibility of the twists) and by comparing localizations of the local ideals across the charts (proof lines 7919-7983). It is H2: the reduction and both inclusions are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the standard relative Proj and twist statements.
